name: Sai Sabzi
ingredients: Fermented bamboo shoots (tuai/chhumi) - 300g, rinsed and sliced
Pork belly (optional but traditional) - 200g, cut into bite-sized pieces
Bird’s eye chilies - 3-4, slit lengthwise (adjust for heat)
Stink beans (petai) - 100g, halved (or substitute with flat beans)
Bamboo shoots (fresh, young) - 200g, thinly sliced (optional for texture)
Wild greens (mizuna or watercress) - 2 cups, roughly chopped
instructions: 1. In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat mustard oil over medium flame until it begins to smoke lightly. Add the pork belly (if using) and sear until golden on all sides.
2. Add crushed garlic, julienned ginger, fresh turmeric, and bird’s eye chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Stir in the fermented bamboo shoots and fresh bamboo slices. Cook for 3-4 minutes, allowing the pungent aroma to mellow.
4. Add the wild mushrooms and stink beans. Toss to coat with the spices, then pour in 3 cups of water (or bone broth for richness).
5. Season with salt and turmeric powder. Bring to a low, rolling boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30 minutes (or 45 minutes if using pork).
6. In the last 5 minutes, stir in the wild greens just until wilted. Adjust salt and chili to taste.
7. Remove from heat, let rest for 5 minutes, and serve steaming hot over steamed rice.
description: A smoky, slow-simmered broth steeped with the earthy tang of fermented bamboo and wild herbs, a taste of Mizoram's hill-slope kitchens.
